the possibility of VEP application for the evaluation of functional asymmetry in patients with mental retardation.
the problem of functional brain asymmetry in patients with different degrees of mental retardation.
a possible role of the functional asymmetry in brain in the pathogenesis of mental retardation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the degree of functional asymmetry is a significant factor in the development of VEP in children with different degrees of mental retardation.
the VEPs in the motor area of the brain reflect a functional asymmetry of the hemispheres in the process of visual information processing in children with different degrees of mental retardation.

in the majority of the patients with intellectual deficiency the functional brain asymmetry was preserved, although in the group of patients with severe mental deficiency the functional brain symmetry was revealed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a functional asymmetry is present in the brain of children with intellectual deficiency, but it is less pronounced than in normal subjects.
a significant correlation has been found between the degree of intellectual deficiency and the functional asymmetry of the brain in the VEP to pattern visual stimuli.
in children with mental retardation a functional asymmetry of the brain is revealed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the functional asymmetry in the visual cortex is a factor of intellectual development.
the degree of functional asymmetry in the brain may influence the development of mental retardation.
the VEP method may be used to study the functional organization of the brain in children with different degrees of mental retardation.
